transcript: Last night, I saw Appropriate by Branden Jacobs-Jenkins on Broadway and I think it was one of the best plays I've seen all year. It’s a family drama where Toni, masterfully played by Sarah Paulson, and her two siblings reconvene in Arkansas to clean up their late father's estate after his passing. But what it's really about is the refusal to take accountability for their family's dark and problematic past as well as their own personal issues. The dialogue is sharp and funny and the family is as dysfunctional as a family can get, exemplified by the scathing insults the siblings hurl at one another. The specificity in the writing is just 🤌 Also the show is thematically very deep and complex but the plot is not hard to follow which my attention span really appreciated on a Wednesday night. I don't wanna give too much else away but the last thing I'll say is that the title of the play is so genius given the multiple meanings of the word appropriate both as an adjective and as a verb. Appropriate is currently running on Broadway at the Hayes through March 3rd, but I bet it'll be extended again. In any case, do not miss this one. With that, another playbill for my collection.
